scope: Proposition 10.1 of the manuscript “Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields” (preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 142 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ed88aa5ba802311a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let E be the largest supplied auxiliary prime, or 2 when none is needed, as in Theorem 1.2. The complete algorithm uses O  B500000 + B100 E20  (10.1) bit operations. The same bound applies if the auxiliary primes are found by upward search and E denotes the largest prime found. In particular, if E = O(B20000000) with an absolute implied constant, the bit cost is O(((n + 1)L)1012 ).
